transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-06-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (recording started at 14:00:12)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Orchid), Priya Rao (Platform Eng - Orchid), Evan Hughes (Product)

Summary: 
Quick scoping call for a 6-week POC to integrate Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoints into Orchid Telecom's internal routing & automated NLU pipelines. Focus on integration approach (SDK vs raw REST), function/tool calling to orchestrate downstream systems, structured JSON output for billing/invoice parsing, benchmarks for 95/99p latency and token cost, and private/VPC deployment constraints. Agreed to run benchmark with Orchid sample traffic; deliverables and owners captured in action items.

Topics: 
- POC scope and timeline
- Workload sizing and benchmark criteria
- SDKs / OpenAI-compat endpoints vs native SDK usage
- Tool/function calling for Orchids' orchestration layer
- Structured output schemas and validation
- Security / private deployment considerations

Transcript: (timestamps approximate; transcription is automated and contains small errors)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Maya and I will run through a proposed POC plan, make sure we capture success criteria and what you need for integration.

[00:18] Liam: Cool, thanks. Concise please, we have a backlog. We're primarily interested in replacing our current hosted completions with something lower-cost and more predictable for peak hours, and—equally—support structured outputs for our billing pipeline.

[00:32] Maya: Great. High level, what Redwood proposes is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for quick integration, SDKs for node/python, plus an option for Private (VPC) deployment if you need isolation. For the POC we usually do a 4-6 week run: onboarding, bench, integration, and success validation.

[00:50] Priya: Quick qualifier: our traffic is spiky. We have 200 req/s at peak for NLU classification and 20 req/s of token-heavy generation for customer-facing flows. Does Redwood handle both on same serving config?

[01:05] Maya: Short answer yes, with routing. We can route classification to a smaller, quantized model or dedicate a pool for large-context generations. We'll want your histogram to size pools properly.

[01:20] Evan: On structured outputs: we have an invoice parser that expects JSON with strict fields: vendor, amount_cents, tax_percent, line_items[]. Can Redwood's function-calling or structured output enforcement support that?

[01:33] Jordan: Absolutely — the OpenAI-compatible function calling is supported and we also have structured schemas you can pin per route. You can validate against the schema and even reject if output doesn't match. Note transcription: sometimes we call it 'functions' or 'tools' interchangeably.

[01:48] Priya: Are those schemas enforced on the server side or client side? We want strong guarantees not just heuristics.

[01:55] Maya: Server-side enforcement is available in Redwood Optimize rules. For the POC we can enable strict mode which returns a 4xx if schema doesn't match and optionally emit an auto-retry with a different prompt template. That helps measure 'structured accuracy' as a success metric.

[02:14] Liam: Ok good. Benchmarks: we need 95th p99 latency targets. Our current SLO is 200ms 95th for classification and 800ms for generation during peak. Can you hit that?

[02:28] Maya: It'll depend on model choice and sequence lengths. For a mid-sized llama-variant quantized we typically see ~120ms 95th for short classifications on A100 pools, and for generation it's model dependent but we can tune batching and KV cache. We'll run a synthetic bench with your sequences to produce a realistic baseline.

[02:45] Evan: And token cost? We need to estimate per-1M token cost if we run 24/7.

[02:50] Jordan: We'll provide cost profiles from Redwood Optimize once bench data is in. For POC planning, we can approximate both hosted (usage-based) and dedicated reserved pool pricing. We can run a side-by-side on the same dataset.

[03:05] Priya: Integration surface: we prefer using our backend Node app. Is the SDK stable? Do you recommend SDK or REST?

[03:14] Maya: Our Node and Python SDKs wrap the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, add built-in telemetry, automatic retries, and multipart streaming helpers. If you need minimal changes, the REST endpoints are drop-in OpenAI compatible; SDK gives faster integration for streaming and function calling.

[03:30] Liam: We have an orchestration layer that calls external tools after parsing. Can Redwood's tool calling orchestrate our internal webhooks or does it only support external predefined tools?

[03:42] Jordan: You can define tool adapters that call your internal endpoints. For private deployments we recommend keeping the adapter inside your network and the model in the private pool. In hosted mode we proxy securely to configured webhook endpoints.

[03:58] Evan: Any caveats around structured outputs when using tool calling? We sometimes see hallucinated keys or loosely typed numbers.

[04:06] Maya: Two mitigations: strict schema enforcement plus reranking with a heuristic layer that validates numeric formats and required fields. We'll show you a quality monitor that flags schema failures and provides diffed examples.

[04:22] Priya: Security: we need SOC2 + KMS integration and don't want tokens stored in third-party logs. Also need VPC peering options.

[04:33] Jordan: We have SOC2 plus optional private deployments that integrate with customer KMS. For logs, you can opt-out of full request body retention; audit logs are configurable. We'll send you the security pack. Maya will follow up with the network diagram we need for VPC peering.

[04:53] Priya: Great. One technical question — what about streaming partial structured output? For UX we sometimes want incremental fields as they arrive.

[05:02] Maya: We support streaming tokens and delta updates for function calls. For structured streaming we can stream chunked JSON patches, but we recommend a final validation step when the full object completes. The SDKs make that easier.

[05:20] Evan: Timeline: you mentioned 4-6 weeks. Can you break down milestones?

[05:26] Jordan: Yep — Week 0 (onboarding + env setup), Week 1 (bench preparatory: collect histograms, sample prompts), Week 2 (bench runs + performance tuning), Week 3-4 (integration + feature test: function calling & structured outputs), Week 5 (quality validations + business metrics), Week 6 (POC wrap, decision + next steps). We can compress to 4 weeks if priority.

[05:50] Liam: Our procurement requires a short trial agreement and an NDA addendum for sample data. Can you accept that?

[05:58] Jordan: Yes, we can sign a trial SOW and the standard NDA addendum. I'll loop in legal after the POC doc is drafted.

[06:07] Priya: About workload sizing: we'll be sending both real-time and batch jobs. Real-time has p95 200ms target; batch jobs can be batched offline. How to account for both in bench?

[06:20] Maya: We'll run separate bench scenarios: one with low-latency single-request flows to measure p95/p99 and one with sustained throughput to emulate batch and measuring cost per token under heavy batching. We'll also surface batching efficiency metrics.

[06:39] Evan: For success criteria, we want a weighted rubric: latency 40%, cost 30%, structured extraction F1 20%, ops friction 10%. Is that reasonable?

[06:48] Jordan: That's a great starting point. We'll draft a formal success criteria doc and include acceptance thresholds for each.

[06:55] Liam: On the bench runs, do you support custom metrics? We have an internal metric called "parser-complete-rate" — percent of invoices parsed without manual review.

[07:05] Maya: Yes, you can add custom metrics. We'll instrument the bench harness to calculate parser-complete-rate using your validation set.

[07:14] Priya: Any gotchas with VPC/on-prem workflow? Latency overhead?

[07:19] Maya: Private deployments add some network and management overhead, but if your model is colocated on the same cloud region, latency delta is modest. The bigger consideration is maintenance windows and cert rotations; we can provide an ops runbook.

[07:33] Evan: Testing — we'd like to run a shadow mode first where Redwood responses are logged but not used in production. Is that supported?

[07:41] Jordan: Yes, shadowing is supported through routing rules and sampling. We'll help configure it so golden traffic continues to your current pipeline while we collect telemetry.

[07:52] Priya: About SDK level telemetry — can we get token-level cost breakdown by route?

[07:58] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. For the POC you'll get a short-term retention view and a CSV export for analysis.

[08:10] Liam: For function calling reliability — if a tool fails, what's Redwood's recommended pattern? Circuit breaker? Retry?

[08:19] Maya: We have built-in retries with exponential backoff and a configurable fallback policy. You can define a circuit-breaker threshold that returns a graceful degraded response. We also support synchronous and async invocation modes for tools.

[08:32] Evan: Good. Any client-side code changes expected? We want minimal dev lift.

[08:37] Jordan: If you use the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, changes are minimal — mostly swapping endpoints and adding the SDK for streaming. For function calling and structured enforcement you might add a small validation shim and error-handling logic.

[08:51] Priya: One more: data residency. Some telecom customer data must remain in-region. Is that supported?

[08:57] Maya: Yes, we offer region pinning on Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can also select region endpoints. We'll capture your region requirements in the onboarding form.

[09:08] Liam: Ok let's recap next steps.

[09:12] Jordan: Action items — Jordan to run bench, Priya to send sample traffic, Maya to share security/VPC docs, Evan and Jordan to draft success criteria doc and SOW. We'll target first bench run by 2025-06-18 and a start of integration in week of 2025-06-23.

[09:30] Priya: Sounds good. Also please include a note on how schema-enforced failures are surfaced to our logs and the retry behavior.

[09:40] Maya: Will do. We'll include examples of schema rejections and the default retry template.

[09:45] Liam: Thanks all. If we get green light from procurement this week we can kick off next Monday.

[09:50] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up with the formal POC doc and signatures. Thanks everyone.

[09:56] (meeting ends)
